obligations.question: Audit deadline lane, initialization, sends, errors, and nesting.
obligations.decision: Retain as-is, evidence verified. Initialization composes inner-first then the own schedule (documented order); errors pass through as the inner B::Error unchanged (policy: no wrapper error type).

obligations.subject: ReceiveTimeout
obligations.question: Audit timer generation, exhaustion, rearming, effects, and nesting.
obligations.decision: Retain as-is, evidence verified. ReceiveTimeout is a Bombay derivation (pure fold + ServiceSends<ScheduleAfter> lane + ReceiveTimeoutEvent sum) with three explicit policies: TimerGeneration disambiguates live vs stale deliveries, only successful continuing user folds rearm (service events never reset inactivity), and generation exhaustion is a controlled ReceiveTimeoutError::GenerationExhausted via checked_add. No lane is dropped, duplicated, reordered, or reinterpreted; the reaction's complete Actions are preserved on firing.

obligations.subject: shutdown wrappers
obligations.question: Audit typed shutdown input and preservation of complete final Actions.
obligations.decision: Retain as-is, evidence verified. Shutdown is a deliberate Bombay policy expressed as an ordinary behavior transition (shutdown.rs module docs), not an actor-model effect. StopOnShutdown stops Normal without running the inner fold; FinalizeOnShutdown retains the final fold's complete sends and creates and replaces only the become verdict with Stop(Normal). ShutdownProtocol adds the ShutdownRequested lane as a closed sum while every inner lane delegates unchanged; init is a pure passthrough and Sends/Ph/Error/Birth are forwarded identically, so no lane is dropped, relabeled, or reinterpreted.

obligations.subject: Stashing
obligations.question: Audit stash routing, replay order, phase constraints, and nesting.
obligations.decision: Retain as-is, evidence verified. Stashing is a Bombay derivation of hold-and-replay over the pure fold: with a pure route function it is an exact filter (derivation, proven against an independent filter model). It uses a single FIFO VecDeque buffer (not two buffers); a local drain batch is the second structure only during replay. Replay preserves arrival order with origins; a mid-drain stop re-extends the remaining batch into held in order. The Ph = Never phase constraint is static (compile-time policy), and non-user service events bypass the stash unrouted, so no lane is dropped, duplicated, reordered, or relabeled in any nesting.

obligations.subject: Fsm
obligations.question: Audit concrete phase/state transitions and static protocol shape.
obligations.decision:
Retain as-is, evidence verified. Fsm is a Bombay derivation solely from receive and become (fsm.rs module doc), not a primitive: typed phases via Move

and Step, with a statically fixed protocol shape (Event = User, Sends = Vec>, Ph = Never, Birth = NoBirths). Deferral replay drains only on a real phase change; the mid-drain merge may reorder held messages but provably never drops or duplicates (|recorded| + held + goto-consumed == stepped at every point). Because User returns None for every service-lane trait, Fsm nests under At/Watching/shutdown wrappers with unmatched service events inert rather than reinterpreted.
